Methods for GeoThinningParameter Objects

Source: R/estimate_thinning_parameter.R
GeoThinningParameter.Rd

Inspect, summarize, extract, and plot the result of estimate_thinning_parameter(). The main result is the named numeric vector `estimated_parameters`; the complete group-level diagnostics are in `estimates`.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'GeoThinningParameter'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GeoThinningParameter'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.GeoThinningParameter'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GeoThinningParameter'
as.data.frame(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GeoThinningParameter'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("auto", "stability", "bdtp"),
  group = NULL,
  resolution = NULL,
  show_replicates = !is.null(x$curves),
  show_ci = TRUE,
  show_threshold = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

A `GeoThinningParameter` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to base graphics or data frame methods.

type

`"auto"`, `"stability"`, or `"bdtp"`. The stability plot shows cumulative-median trajectories; the BD-TP plot shows SVM training data, the decision boundary, and predictions. The default is based on the fitted method.

group

Optional group to plot. If `NULL`, the first group with an available trajectory is used. In BD-TP plots, selected groups are highlighted.

resolution

Candidate resolutions to show in stability plots. If `NULL`, all available resolutions are plotted.

show_replicates

Show individual trajectories if `keep_curves = TRUE`.

show_ci

Show the summarized trajectory interval.

show_threshold

Show the stabilization threshold and

Value

`print()` and `plot()` return the input object invisibly. `summary()` returns a compact summary object. `as.data.frame()` returns the complete `estimates` table.

Details

For LS-TP, `print()` and `summary()` report how many groups reached stability. When no tested resolution is stable, the function returns 0.001 degrees as a default value. This does not mean that stability was achieved.

For BD-TP, the results indicate whether a predicted resolution was limited to the minimum of 0.001 degrees or falls outside the tested resolution range. BD-TP estimates resolutions from geographical range size, so its predictions are not necessarily among those tested.

Stability plots show the summarized cumulative-median trajectories, even when individual replicate curves were not saved. If there are too few environmental observations to calculate a trajectory, an informative message is displayed.

In BD-TP plots, overlapping training points are slightly separated to make them visible. This adjustment affects only the plot, not the underlying data, fitted model, or predicted resolutions. Plotting is reproducible and does not use random numbers.
